solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lifeguards caught cavorting? Outrageous!

indicators.note: cavorting is leaping about wildly, so these letters prance into a new order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is scandalised at lifeguards larking about together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' tells you to shuffle LIFEGUARDS plus C.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disgraceful is shocking enough to make people exclaim at it, a close synonym of outrageous.

clue.text: Gloomy Democrat given the boot

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics
given the boot means thrown out, ejected

explanation.surface: A politician turned out of office feels low.
explanation.definitionFit: Dejected means downcast and low in spirits, a synonym of gloomy.

clue.text: Philosopher needing help to collect old banger

indicators.note: to collect means to take something in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: SOS is the distress call asking for help
a crate is slang for a decrepit old car, as is banger in Britain

explanation.surface: A thinker calls for assistance to pick up a clapped-out car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' is British slang for an old car (also a sausage); SOS 'to collect' CRATE gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the ancient Athenian thinker who founded Western philosophy.

clue.text: Heretic's dance entertaining bishop

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting a guest, so one word is taken inside another

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A heretic dances while a bishop watches.
explanation.walkthrough: REEL 'entertaining' B gives REBEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic defies accepted doctrine, so is a rebel against the established church.

clue.text: Who will investigate if singer gets run down?

indicators.note: down in a down clue means the letter is shifted lower, further along the word

parts.note: a crooner is a singer of sentimental songs
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A question about who looks into it if a singer is knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: In CROONER the R (run) 'gets... down', moving one place later to give CORONER; the surface's road accident is also what such an officer would investigate.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner is the official who inquires into sudden or unexplained deaths.

clue.text: Priests who've not been celibate?

parts.note: Catholic priests are addressed by one title, which is also the word for men who have had children

explanation.surface: A question about clergy who have broken their vow of chastity.
explanation.walkthrough: Priests are called Father; those who have not been celibate may literally be dads.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both priests by title and male parents, the second implying they were not celibate.

clue.text: Alec's rant upset royal house

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alec's angry tirade offends the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' shuffles ALECS RANT.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Lancaster was an English royal dynasty in the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Cockney's shock appearance

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker famously drops the initial aitch, so the word loses its H

parts.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair

explanation.surface: A London speaker gets a fright at how something looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' reads as a fright but means a mop of HAIR; Cockneys, London's working-class East Enders, drop their aitches, leaving AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a manner or outward look, as in having an air of confidence.

clue.text: Bitter investigators in US agency sent north

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other
in a down answer, sent north means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
CID is the British police Criminal Investigation Department

explanation.surface: Resentful detectives posted inside an American agency are transferred north.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'sent north' means read upwards; the British detectives sit just after the first letter of the reversed agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic means sharp and sour in taste, or biting in manner, close to bitter.

clue.text: Guide had a word with Charles's mum

parts.note: rang means telephoned, had a word with someone on the phone
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was King Charles's mother

explanation.surface: A tour guide phones the King's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guide' points to a scout; a Ranger is an older member of the Girl Guides, a British youth movement, as well as a forest guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranger guides visitors through a park, and in Britain Rangers are senior Girl Guides.

clue.text: Rees-Mogg is such a woolly individual

definitions.text: Rees-Mogg is such a woolly individual

parts.words: Rees-Mogg is such a woolly individual
parts.note: the politician's first name is also a breed of spotted, horned sheep, a woolly creature

explanation.surface: A jibe that a well-known Tory politician is vague and muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob Rees-Mogg is a British Conservative politician; a Jacob is also a breed of sheep, so 'woolly' is literal, not 'vague'.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed of piebald sheep shares its name with the politician's forename, so either reading fits.

clue.text: Keeping form of punishment new head introduced

indicators.note: a fresh first letter is put in place of the original opening letter

parts.note: detention is a school punishment of being kept in

explanation.surface: A school keeping pupils in after a new headteacher arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new head introduced' swaps the D at the front of DETENTION for R.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention is the act of holding on to something, the noun sense of keeping.

clue.text: What might follow university? It's a problem

definitions.meaning: University ... is a long-running British TV quiz for student teams

explanation.surface: A remark about what comes after a degree being difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes the quiz show's title and also means a demanding task to overcome.

clue.text: Teacher back in Casualty in spring

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, the hospital department holding the teacher

parts.note: A and E (Accident and Emergency) is the British hospital casualty department

indicators.note: back means the word for a teacher is read from right to left

parts.note: sir is how British pupils address a male teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher returns to hospital work in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SIR into RIS, which goes 'in' A&E, the British emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise or spring up both mean to come into being or emerge suddenly.

clue.text: Reportedly the first person to use Ray-Bans?

indicators.note: reportedly signals a phrase heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: the first person pronoun saying they use clothing gives I wear

explanation.surface: A question about who first wore a famous brand of sunglasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first person to use' is 'I wear' (I being the first person), and said aloud that is EYEWEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ray-Bans are a famous brand of sunglasses, an example of spectacles and shades; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: A moonlit scene ultimately making you sentimental

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter is taken
making means forming something out of the material, so these letters are built into a new order

explanation.surface: A romantic moonlit scene leaves you misty-eyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes E, the end of scene, which leads the answer; 'making' turns A MOONLIT into MOTIONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional means moved by feelings, readily stirred, which is what sentimental describes.

clue.text: Third son's name registered in Somerset House

indicators.note: the name is recorded inside the words that follow, spanning them

explanation.surface: A birth record held at the old London register office.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset House in London once held England's birth registers, which makes 'registered in' a neat hiding signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Seth is Adam and Eve's third son, after Cain and Abel.

clue.text: Sack everyone blocking women's online protection

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
W is the abbreviation for women
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Dismissing staff who obstruct women's internet safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' is a link here: ALL comes after W, which also hints at what a firewall does.
explanation.definitionFit: A firewall is software that blocks unauthorised network traffic, a computer security barrier.

clue.text: Bachelor lounged about in club

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a degree

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A single man lounged around at his club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a gentlemen's club; it is a heavy stick. 'about' shuffles LOUNGED.
explanation.definitionFit: A bludgeon is a short heavy stick used as a weapon, a cudgel or club.

clue.text: Sound of river provoking cries of wonder

indicators.note: sound of signals that the word is heard aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England, pronounced like ooze

explanation.surface: The noise of flowing water stirs people to amazement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse, a river in Yorkshire and elsewhere in England, is said 'ooze', which sounds like OOHS.
explanation.definitionFit: Oohs are the drawn-out exclamations people make when amazed or delighted.

clue.text: Exclude contrary American while away

indicators.note: contrary means turned the opposite way, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: to while away time is to spend it

explanation.surface: Shutting out an awkward American who is off travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' turns US into SU.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend a pupil or player is to bar them temporarily, which excludes them.

clue.text: Biased and incomplete

definitions.meaning: ... also means only in part, not whole

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective has both senses: showing favouritism, and covering only some of something.

clue.text: Introduce Penny to shrink

parts.note: to recede is to diminish or draw back

explanation.surface: Presenting Penny to a psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrink' looks like a psychiatrist noun; it is the verb RECEDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede something is to come before it, as a preface or opener does in introducing it.

clue.text: Shifty-looking yob briefly taking heroin in church

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a yob is a lout, British slang for a thug

indicators.note: in means one piece sits within another

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A shady thug uses drugs inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts LOUT to LOU; H goes 'in' CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche means disreputable in a raffish way, describing a dubious, shady-looking character.

clue.text: Sex with American in limo? It'll cost you

indicators.note: in means these pieces are placed within the vehicle

parts.note: a limo is a luxury car
sex is Latin for six, VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Romance in the back of a limousine with an American comes at a price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex' is Latin for six, VI; VI and A go 'in' CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviar is famously expensive sturgeon roe, the classic luxury food that costs a lot.

clue.text: Chap from Middle East retiring very soon

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, so the phrase goes backwards

parts.note: in a mo, short for in a moment, means very soon

explanation.surface: A man from the Gulf is about to stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reverses IN A MO.
explanation.definitionFit: An Omani is a native of Oman, a country on the Arabian Peninsula in the Middle East.

clue.text: S for pioneer?

parts.note: the letter S is what begins the weapon's name, its head, so it stands for that start

explanation.surface: Reads like a phonetic alphabet entry: S stands for pioneer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: the 'head' of SPEAR is the letter S, which is just what the clue shows.
explanation.definitionFit: To spearhead is to lead an advance; as a noun a spearhead is the person at the front, a leader or pioneer.

clue.text: Run over MP, losing head at last

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: a redcap is British slang for a military policeman

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of the word is the one used

explanation.surface: A politician is knocked down and finally loses their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'MP' looks like a Member of Parliament but is Military Police, a REDCAP; it loses D, the last of 'head'.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to go over the main points again, which is to run over them.

clue.text: One's patrons tell niece off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone tells their niece to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' shuffles TELL NIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: A business's clientele are its regular customers, the patrons it serves.

clue.text: Stop patient swallowing a drug

indicators.note: swallowing means one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a doctor's case is a patient
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A doctor tells a patient to stop taking pills.
explanation.walkthrough: CASE 'swallowing' E (ecstasy) gives CEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to come to an end or halt, a direct synonym for stop.

clue.text: Royal couple go astray

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of the late Queen
her other half in the royal couple is R, for Rex the king

explanation.surface: A king and queen wander off the right path.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal couple is ER and R, queen and king.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake or wander from the right course.

clue.text: Group piloted an aircraft once

parts.note: to pilot is to guide or lead, past tense led
a zeppelin is an early German airship, no longer flown

explanation.surface: A historical note that someone flew an early airship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' looks like a squadron; it is the rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Led Zeppelin were a famous British rock band, and a band is a musical group.
